step1_analysis.description: A differential pair with tied collectors. When driven differentially, the fundamental frequency cancels at the output while the even harmonics (primarily the 2nd harmonic) add constructively, effectively doubling the input frequency.

paper_reference.title: SiGe W-CDMA Transmitter for Mobile Terminal Application

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the circuit from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. Assuming 1k load and bias of 0.9V, I_total ~ 1.8mA. P = 1.8V * 1.8mA = 3.24mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports the power for the entire transmitter IC. This single sub-block will consume significantly less power, determined by the bias resistors.

conversion_gain.description: Voltage gain from the fundamental input frequency to the 2nd harmonic output frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Vout_2nd / Vin_fund. Push-push doublers typically exhibit conversion loss unless actively buffered.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the transconductance of the BJTs and the load resistor R1.

fundamental_rejection.description: Suppression of the fundamental frequency at the output relative to the 2nd harmonic.

sky130_expected.calculation: 20 * log10(Vout_fund / Vout_2nd). Relies on the matching of the differential pair.
sky130_expected.reasoning: In a perfectly matched SPICE simulation, rejection is extremely high. In reality, mismatches limit it to ~40 dBc.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power consumption and transient conversion gain of the push-push frequency doubler.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Push-Push Frequency Doubler Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Define generic NPN model since SKY130 NPNs have different subcircuit names
.model npn npn (bf=100 is=1e-15 vaf=50)

* DUT (with component values added for simulation)
Q1 n0 label_net_0 n2 npn
Q2 n0 n1 n2 npn
C1 n2 label_net_1 10p
R1 VDD n0 1k
R2 n2 GND 1k
C2 n1 label_net_2 10p

* Biasing and Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8

* Differential RF input at 1GHz (0.1V peak)
Vbias0 label_net_0 0 dc 0.9 sin(0.9 0.1 1G 0 0 0)
Vbias2 label_net_2 0 dc 0.9 sin(0.9 0.1 1G 0 0 180)

* AC ground for emitter bypass
Vbias1 label_net_1 0 dc 0

* DC Bias for n1 (AC coupled via C2)
Vbias_n1 n1_dc 0 dc 0.9
Rbias n1 n1_dc 100k

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point for Power Consumption
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* 2. Transient Analysis for Conversion Gain (2nd Harmonic)
tran 10p 5n
* Measure peak-to-peak output voltage at steady state
meas tran vout_max max v(n0) from=3n to=5n
meas tran vout_min min v(n0) from=3n to=5n
let vout_pp = vout_max - vout_min

* Input is 0.1V peak differential, so single-ended amplitude is 0.1V (0.2Vpp)
let conversion_gain = vout_pp / 0.2
print vout_pp conversion_gain

quit
.endc
